---
title: "Writing a Backend"
guide-section: "Advanced"
---

For contributors adding a system tether does not know yet. A backend maps
tether's operations onto one class of system. One instance serves every
object of its kind, and per-object addressing travels in the `locator`.
Implement the `ObjectBackend` protocol (`tether.backends.base`), register
it, and run the conformance suite. This page also defines the capability
flags, and what *experimental* means for a backend.

## The protocol

```python
from tether.backends import Capability, ObjectBackend, ObjectDiff, VerifyReport, VerifyStatus, register_backend
from tether.handles import Handle
from tether.manifest import Locator, Pin, State, ref_for_pin


class MyBackend(ObjectBackend):
    kind = "mysys"
    capabilities = (
        Capability.FINGERPRINT | Capability.ADDRESSABLE | Capability.PIN | Capability.FORK
        | Capability.ATOMIC_REF | Capability.DIFF
    )

    def __init__(self, config: dict | None = None) -> None:
        self._config = config or {}          # [backends.mysys] from tether.toml

    def identity(self, locator: Locator) -> Locator: ...
    def fingerprint(self, locator: Locator, working_ref: str | None) -> State: ...
    def pin(self, locator: Locator, state: State, pin_id: str) -> Pin: ...
    def unpin(self, locator: Locator, pin: Pin) -> None: ...
    def list_pins(self, locator: Locator) -> set[str]: ...
    def verify(self, locator: Locator, state: State, pin: Pin | None, deep: bool) -> VerifyReport: ...
    def fork(self, locator: Locator, source: Pin | State, name: str, *, expected: State | None = None) -> str: ...
    def delete_working_ref(self, locator: Locator, ref: str) -> None: ...
    def open(self, locator: Locator, target: str | Pin | State | None, read_only: bool) -> Handle: ...


register_backend("mysys", lambda config: MyBackend(config))
```

Method by method:

| Method | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `identity(locator)` | The subset of the locator that names the *system* (not the branch, region, or credential references). It is hashed into the pin id, so two objects with the same identity and state share a pin. Pass a local path through `canonical_uri`, so every spelling of one directory is one identity. |
| `fingerprint(locator, working_ref)` | The current state at `working_ref` (a branch `fork` returned) or at the locator's base ref when `None`. Must be a JSON-compatible dict whose *content* keys are stable across calls when nothing changed and different after any change. Keys that merely address the data (an LSN, a derived id) go in `VOLATILE_KEYS` so `content_state` excludes them from equality and pin ids; never include coordinates that move on unrelated activity (Iceberg's `metadata_location`). |
| `VOLATILE_KEYS` (class attribute) | State keys that address but do not identify: excluded from drift detection, pin ids, listing names, and export hashes; still passed to `pin` / `open` / `verify`. Default: none. |
| `pin(locator, state, pin_id)` | Create the native ref `ref_for_pin(pin_id)` (`tether.<id>`) pointing at `state`. The id is opaque to the backend (`<dataset8>.<hash16>`; the engine namespaces it). Idempotent: if it exists and points at the same state, return it; if it points elsewhere, raise `BackendError`. Raise if the state is no longer reachable -- `repair` relies on that. |
| `unpin(locator, pin)` | Delete the ref. A ref that is already gone is a no-op or a `BackendError`, never a library exception. |
| `list_pins(locator)` | Pin ids (without the `tether.` prefix) that exist natively, every dataset's included. The engine keeps only its own namespace before `gc` subtracts the referenced ones. |
| `verify(locator, state, pin, deep)` | With a pin: `OK` if it resolves to `state`, `DRIFTED` if it points elsewhere, `MISSING` if gone. Without: `UNKNOWN` unless `deep`, then actually open the state. |
| `fork(locator, source, name, *, expected=None)` | Create writable branch `name` and return the working ref (usually `name`; a backend may pick a sibling if `name` is taken). `source` is a `Pin`, or a recorded `State` for `pin = "record"` objects (raise `BackendError` if it is no longer reachable). **Reset contract**: an existing `name` is moved back onto `source` (a reset, a ref update, a branch restore, delete-and-recreate), and left alone when it is already there; conformance checks it. **Conditional move**: `expected` is the head the caller reviewed, a `State` or `ABSENT`; anything else raises `RefMovedError` and moves nothing. Use the system's compare-and-swap where it has one (git `update-ref <new> <old>`, Icechunk `reset_branch(from_snapshot_id=)`) and declare `CONDITIONAL_REF`; elsewhere call `check_expected(self, locator, expected, ref=name)` first. `None` moves unconditionally. A signature without the keyword is called without it, and the engine warns that its moves are unconditional. |
| `delete_working_ref(locator, ref)` | Delete a branch `fork` created; never the base branch. Ignore "already gone". |
| `working_ref_blockers(locator, ref)` | Why `ref` cannot be deleted right now, or `None`. `gc --prune-bookmarks` / `forget-workspace` plan a blocked branch as kept with the reason instead of failing at apply. Neon: pin children. Default: none. |
| `rename_pin(locator, old, state, new_id)` | Give an existing pin a new id (`tether upgrade` when the naming scheme changes). Default: `pin` the state under the new id, then `unpin` the old -- right wherever pins are tags. Override where a pin is a branch with children (Neon renames in place). |
| `rename_working_ref(locator, old, new)` | Rename a working branch; return the resulting ref. Default: `fork` `new` from `old`'s head state and delete `old`. |
| `list_working_refs(locator)` | Native branches named `tether.ws.*` (`WORKING_REF_PREFIX`) in this system, every dataset's included; the engine filters to its own namespace. `gc --prune-bookmarks` fingerprints each stray one and deletes it only if its head is pinned or equals the base head (`--force-prune` overrides); `repair` uses it to notice a missing working branch. Default: none. |
| `promote(locator, source, *, expected=None)` | `PROMOTE`: fast-forward the base branch to `source` (a working ref, `Pin`, or `State`); refuse with `BackendError` unless the base head is an ancestor of it, and no-op when already there. Return the base's new state. `expected` is the base head the plan reviewed: raise `RefMovedError` when the base holds another state, through the compare-and-swap where there is one, else `check_expected(self, locator, expected, what="promote")` first. |
| `merge(locator, source, message, *, expected=None)` | `MERGE`: three-way merge `source` into the base; raise `MergeConflict(conflicts=[...])` and leave the base untouched on conflicts. Return the base's new state. The engine passes the *state* the plan reviewed, so merge that commit, not the branch head. Check `expected` with `check_expected(self, locator, expected, what="merge")` first: merges have no old-value form. |
| `ancestor_of(locator, ancestor, descendant)` | Whether `ancestor` (a state) is in `descendant`'s history; `None` when unknown. `promote` falls back to it when no fork point was recorded. |
| `PROMOTE_HINT` (class attribute) | The sentence `promote` shows when it refuses: what the user should do with the system's own tools. |
| `open(locator, target, read_only)` | `target` is `None` (base ref), a `str` working ref, a `Pin` (read the pinned state), or a `State` (read an Addressable state). Return a `Handle` subclass carrying the native address and, where cheap, a native object. |
| `create(locator, *, owner)` | `CREATE`: make an empty store at the locator, write an owner marker *in the store* naming `owner` (a dataset id), and return the initial state. Raise `BackendError` if anything is already there -- `create` never adopts. |
| `owner(locator)` | `CREATE`: the dataset id in the store's owner marker; `None` when tether never wrote one or the store is gone. |
| `is_ref_empty(locator, *, ignoring=())` | `CREATE`: `True` when nothing remains but the base branch at its initial state, the marker, and the refs in `ignoring` (the ones a gc plan is about to delete) -- and, for a store with a working area (a git checkout, a directory), no uncommitted content: files are data whether or not a ref names them; `False` otherwise; `None` when the backend cannot tell. `None` means keep. |
| `delete_store(locator)` | `CREATE`: remove the store. Called only after `is_ref_empty` returned `True` and `owner` named the caller's dataset -- and expected to check both again itself, right before the irreversible step, and to remove only what the store's own layout accounts for. |

The owner marker is the whole basis for a delete: manifests travel with
clones and are untrusted, so a manifest field never authorizes one. Put the
marker where the store keeps its own metadata (Icechunk repository metadata,
`git config`, a `.tether-owner` file the directory walk skips) -- never in a
ref that `list_pins` or `list_working_refs` would report.

`pin` must be idempotent *and say which it did*: return `Pin(..., created=True)`
when it made the ref, `created=False` when it found the ref already carrying
the state. `commit` rolls back only the pins it created; a reused one belongs
to the commit that made it. `unpin` and `delete_working_ref` must raise
`BackendError` when the ref is still there afterwards -- "already gone" is
success, a refused deletion is not.

Optional members:

- `effective_capabilities(locator, policy) -> Capability` when the tier varies
  per object (the `file` backend is Observed for a local directory and
  Addressable for a versioned remote object).
- `MATURITY` (class attribute, default `"stable"`): `"experimental"` when the
  backend is tested against a fake of a network service rather than the
  service itself. `tether backends` prints it; `add` mentions it.
- `LOCAL_PATH_KEYS` (class attribute): locator keys that may hold a local
  filesystem path, after any of `LOCAL_PATH_PREFIXES` (DuckLake's
  `ducklake:`, `sqlite:`, ...). At `add`/`import` the engine expands a
  leading `~` and resolves a relative path against the caller's directory,
  so a committed locator means one path from every directory and clone.
- `branch_scope(locator) -> str` and `ref_namespace(locator) -> str` when the
  native resource that owns branches, or the one whose pins `list_pins`
  returns, is wider than one object -- a Neon project, an Iceberg table. The
  engine forks one branch per scope under a bookmark (members `share` it)
  and collects `gc` references per namespace. Both default to the canonical
  identity.
- `state_addressable(locator, state) -> bool` (default `True`) when an
  Addressable backend can produce a state that nonetheless has no coordinate
  to reopen it by (a `file` object in a bucket without versioning has no
  `version_id`). `commit` records such a state `recoverable = false`.
- `check_quiescence(locator, working_ref)` for `NEEDS_QUIESCENCE` backends;
  raise `BackendError` if writers are active.
- `listing(locator, state) -> str | None` and
  `diff(locator, a, b, *, listings) -> ObjectDiff` for `DIFF` (below).
- `history(locator, ref, limit) -> list[HistoryEntry]` for `HISTORY`: the
  system's native history newest first (`id`, ISO `when`, `message`, `refs`).
  Each `id` must be accepted as the locator's `at` field, and `fingerprint`
  must honor `at` (via `base_at(locator)`) when no working ref is given, so
  users can register an object at any listed state.

Raise `BackendError` (or `CapabilityError` for unsupported operations) with
`kind=self.kind`; the engine aggregates per-object failures into
`MultiObjectError`. Import optional libraries *inside* methods, so the
module imports without them. Decorate the class with `@wrap_library_errors`
and give it a `_library_errors()` staticmethod returning the library's
exception types, which every protocol method then re-raises as
`BackendError`. The decorator wraps only methods *defined on the class*, so
re-declare an inherited one. `validate_locator` runs the checks that are
cheap at `add` time, so a refusal reaches the manifest's author, not the
first reader of a clone.

## Capabilities decide behavior

Declare only what the system truly supports; the engine degrades explicitly.

| Capability | The engine will... |
| --- | --- |
| `FINGERPRINT` | `fingerprint` (required) |
| `ADDRESSABLE` | let `open(state)` read a recorded state without a pin |
| `PIN` | call `pin` on commit, `list_pins`/`unpin` in `gc`, `verify` with the pin. Removed per object by `policy.pin = "record"`, in which case commit records the state instead |
| `FORK` | call `fork` in `new` (from the pin, or from the recorded state without one) and return writable handles from `open`; `list_working_refs`/`delete_working_ref` in `gc --prune-bookmarks` |
| `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT` | (informational) metadata-only reads |
| `RETENTION_BOUND` | (informational) surface that recoverability expires |
| `NEEDS_QUIESCENCE` | call `check_quiescence` before pinning |
| `ATOMIC_REF` | (informational) pins are create-if-absent |
| `CONDITIONAL_REF` | trust that `fork`, and `promote` / `merge` where declared, honour `expected` in one atomic step. Declare it only then; `effective_capabilities` can declare it per object (Icechunk: on `s3://` only). Conformance runs 8 racing forks and fails a backend that declares it and ignores `expected`. |
| `DIFF` | call `diff` for `diff --content`, `listing` at commit |
| `HISTORY` | call `history` for `tether log` and `add --pick` |
| `BRANCH_IS_STORAGE` | never delete a stray working branch in `gc --prune-bookmarks` without `--force-prune` (deleting reclaims the data, as in Neon) |
| `PROMOTE` | call `promote` in `tether promote` when the base is unchanged since the fork point |
| `MERGE` | call `merge` in `tether promote` when the base moved (or `--strategy merge`) |
| `CREATE` | *(experimental)* call `create` for `add --create` / `Repo.create`; `owner`, `is_ref_empty`, and `delete_store` in `gc --delete-stores` for a created store nothing references any more (`tether.experimental.lifecycle`) |

## Content diffs and listings

`diff(locator, a, b, *, listings)` returns an `ObjectDiff`: a `unit` naming
what is counted (files, tables, arrays, ...), exact `added`/`removed`/
`modified` counts, and entries (capped at 2000; use `out.add(path, change,
detail)`). Read metadata only; never data.

If your state is a digest that cannot be diffed on its own, also implement
`listing(locator, state)`, returning a detailed text description (JSON
lines work well). The engine commits it under `.tether/listings/` and hands
both sides back as `listings=(text_a, text_b)`. Degrade to a summary line
when either is `None`.

## Experimental and graduation

Backends driven only through fakes of their service (Neon, Dolt, DuckLake,
Iceberg) and the registry layer live under `tether.experimental`:

```
tether/experimental/backends/{neon,dolt,ducklake,iceberg}.py
tether/experimental/registry/{export,registry}.py
```

**What is stable.** Kind names (`tether add --kind neon`), extras
(`tether-vcs[neon]`), the CLI commands, the `Repo` methods (`repo.export()`,
`plan_import`, `apply_import`, `import_objects`), and the `tether.<Symbol>`
re-exports (`ExportBundle`, `ImportSpec`, `ImportReport`, `PublishReport`,
`build_bundle`, `specs_from_rows`). These do not change when something
graduates. Module paths under `tether.experimental` are *not* API, and the
alpha-era paths (`tether.backends.neon`, `tether.export`, `tether.registry`)
are gone.

**It is a real boundary.** `import tether` and `import tether.cli` load
nothing under `tether.experimental.registry`. The `Repo` methods import it
on first call, the `tether.<Symbol>` names resolve lazily, and
`tether.experimental.cli.register(app)` attaches the three CLI commands.

**What "experimental" means.** The backend passes the conformance suite and
its engine lifecycle against a fake, not the service. `tether backends`
reports `experimental`, and `tether add` prints a note. What only a live run
can confirm (rate limits, eventual consistency, what a protected branch
costs) remains to be seen.

**Graduation is a file move.** `build_backend` resolves a kind through
`_BUILTIN_MODULES`, and the class's `MATURITY` drives the label. Move the
file to `tether/backends/`, point its `_BUILTIN_MODULES` entry there, set
`MATURITY = "stable"`, and update the table in [Backends](09-backends.qmd).
Nothing users type or import changes. The registry graduates the same way,
keeping the `tether` re-exports. `ROADMAP.md` has each backend's call.

## Conformance suite

`tether.testing.run_conformance` runs the tier-appropriate checks against any
backend. Provide a harness that can create a fresh system and mutate it:

```python
from tether.backends import ObjectBackend
from tether.manifest import Locator
from tether.testing import run_conformance


class MyHarness:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.backend: ObjectBackend = MyBackend()
        self._n = 0

    def new_object(self) -> Locator:
        ...  # create an empty system with a `main` branch; return its locator

    def mutate(self, locator: Locator, working_ref: str | None) -> None:
        self._n += 1
        ...  # write something new at working_ref (or the base branch)

    def fresh_locator(self) -> Locator:  # CREATE backends only
        ...  # a locator where no store exists yet


def test_conformance() -> None:
    run_conformance(MyHarness())
```

What the suite checks, per capability:

- **Always:** fingerprint stability and change, identity and pin-id
  determinism, and unpin.
- **`DIFF`:** an empty self-diff, and a non-empty one after a mutation.
- **`HISTORY`:** the newest entry is the current state and works as `at`,
  an older entry is another state, and `limit` bounds the result.
- **`ADDRESSABLE`:** open by state, an older recorded state included.
- **`PIN`:** create, list, verify shallow and deep, idempotency, and
  protection against later drift of the working ref.
- **`FORK`:** a fresh fork equals the pinned state, and writes to it leave
  the base alone. A stale `expected`, or `ABSENT` onto an existing branch,
  raises `RefMovedError` and moves nothing.
- **`CONDITIONAL_REF`:** of 8 threads forking with one `expected`, exactly
  one moves the branch; the backend must take `expected`.
- **`PROMOTE` and `MERGE`:** the base follows the fork, a second promote is
  a no-op, a base that moved is refused, two diverged sides merge, and a
  stale `expected` is refused. `ancestor_of` answers in the right direction,
  or `None`.
- **`CREATE`:** the store lifecycle at a `fresh_locator()`, from `create`
  through `owner`, `is_ref_empty` (with and without `ignoring`) and a second
  `create` refused, to `delete_store` and a `create` that works again.

A harness may set `capabilities` to exercise one tier of a multi-tier
backend. `tether.backends.memory` is the executable specification the suite
was written against. `tether.backends.lance` is a Forkable backend that had
to bend the mapping (branch-scoped versions, undeletable tagged branches)
without breaking the contract.

## VCS adapters

Three members beyond reading and committing files. `history_digest()`
digests every visible commit id, so a commit made in another workspace
stales a gc plan. `shared_dir()` names the directory every checkout of the
repository shares (git's common dir, jj's repo dir), where the repository
lock and the pinned, created and touched indexes live. `tracked(paths)`
says which of tether's per-checkout files the VCS tracks, so `find` can
refuse a clone that ships them.

Backends never touch the VCS. If you need to support another version-control
system for the *manifests*, implement `tether.vcs.VcsAdapter` (resolve, read
and list files at a revision, stream history, commit, new) and extend
`detect_vcs`. The jj and git adapters read history through one
`git cat-file --batch` process (`GitObjectReader`); a non-git store should aim
for the same batching to keep `gc` and `verify --all-history` fast.
